title: DRT-Assisted Evaluation of the Corrosion Inhibition of Vanillin on AA6082-T6 Aluminum Alloy
content: The possibility to use vanillin for corrosion inhibition of AA6082-T6 aluminum alloy in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution was investigated using AC/DC electrochemical techniques and quantitative metallography. DRT deconvolution demonstrated that uninhibited alloy dissolution is governed by mass-transfer-dominated mixed control, whereas vanillin adsorption preferentially blocks cathodic Al15(Fe,Mn)3Si2 and AlMnSi inclusions, shifting the corrosion process toward activation control. Pre-saturation adsorption obeyed the Langmuir isotherm with R2 = 0.9906 and free energy of adsorption of +27.63 kJ mol1, confirming mixed physisorption and chemisorption thermodynamically reinforced by electrolyte salting-out. At the optimal concentration of 1.0516 × 102 mol dm3, vanillin formed a protective 3D organic/inorganic interphase layer via bidentate chelation inside oxide pores and donor–acceptor coordination on Fe/Mn sites, reaching maximum inhibition efficiency of 82.94%. At higher concentration protection decreased to 71.82% due to supramolecular aggregation, a flat-to-vertical orientational transition, and ligand-promoted dissolution. Post-polarization surface analysis revealed that localized attack propagates radially along sub-grain boundaries, forming acidic occluded cells that sterically exclude bulky vanillin aggregates and prevent spontaneous repassivation.
